title: Prove a sharp dense-bypass rank floor for Gaussian fusion (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration, produced by Nick Petalas. A dense bypass around one flat Gaussian child must retain almost the full target matrix rank when rectangular adapter norms are bounded.

```text
T = B K A + H + E
T: d-dimensional unitary; K: N-dimensional flat unitary
rank_C(H)=h; ||E||_(2->2)<=eta<1
M=||A||_1 ||B||_infinity

(d-h)(1-eta)^2 <= ||BKA||_F^2 <= d^2 M^2/N
```

The bypass may touch every entry and have unbounded coefficients. An orthonormal basis of its kernel proves the lower energy bound. An explicit Gaussian family attains both inequalities, proving the constant sharp.

For two independent width-f targets and one rank-two child, exact output with M<=1 requires `h >= 2*2^f-4`. If the dense bypass has rank at most `2^f`, then `M >= (1-eta)*2^((r-1)f/2)/sqrt(2)`. Here h is complex coordinate-matrix rank, distinct from recursive axis rank. No new kappa or selected-frontier change.

## Evidence

- Before: ToikY [#7166](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7166), exact model head `6efb5d028b3212fba68edfb725608413622d6ab6`, supplies the rectangular Gaussian normalization and column-sparse bypass test. A dense rank-one bypass need not leave a missing entry. Its scientific verifier and invoice were not replayed.
- After: `PROOF.md` supplies the kernel/energy argument and sharp Gaussian construction. The exact Q(i) verifier checks four flat unitary children, 28 equality witnesses, 48 additional adapter fixtures, two full-child controls and 14 rejecting controls.
- CPython 3.12.15 warning-strict normal and optimized direct runs passed in 0.94 seconds each. Generated six-file hash-bound receipts agree byte for byte. Both registered commands passed locally, individually below their 120-second limits.
- Source compilation, metadata/provenance pins, exact committed bytes, executable modes and declared source ancestry passed. The official six-file export passed integrity checking; read-only Git-free normal/optimized exported replays passed with matching receipts.

## Limitations and credit

The universal statement rests on the written proof. Finite error fixtures use E=eta*T; the theorem allows arbitrary operator-norm error. The constant is attained at rank deficit one, without claiming attainability for every prescribed h and M. Coordinate rank is not an implementation bill. The witness has dense, almost full-rank bypass, with no physical cost advantage claimed.

Physical allocation, dirty restoration, routing, native adaptation, precision/tape costs, a complete supplier invoice and multiplication theorem remain unproved. No selected cold replay, Lean or Docker run was performed. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

Credit ToikY #7166; Clear1nsight #4932/#4045/#3989; Rohan Arun #7113; and the retained Gaussian native, controller and compiler lineage. The general matrix inequalities are elementary classical facts. The new dense-bypass application, attaining family and verifier were produced by Nick Petalas. No predecessor code or external scientific data is imported.

Canonical base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`, priority revision 8, selected #7000. The `coverage-law-change` card changes to a local dense-bypass obstruction. [Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19541804). Only the six-file package is added.

## Open next questions

- Bind an actual eligible bypass to a coordinate-rank cap. Start with its literal input/output spaces and charge every bypass, adapter and restoration operation before claiming a complete obstruction or gain.
- Determine the constrained optimum at a prescribed M and rank deficit greater than one. The sharp constant alone does not settle every such point.

- [#7244](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7244) proposes a different complete paid word; this theorem is a standalone local contract.

The completion refresh checked this account's nine other open PRs created since the CLAIM, #7247 through #7255. Only #7249 studies this Gaussian-fusion interface; its line above records the different bypass constraint and error metric. No shared numerical optimum is computed by both results.

These lines compare published contracts only. No extra computation checked another contribution's numbers.
